Qu'est-ce que Cartes.gouv.fr, l'outil de la France pour concurrencer Google Maps et Street View

2026-07-14 Maxime Escot (L'Éveil de la Haute-Loire) IGN, Cartes.gouv.fr, Géoportail, Google Maps, Street View, Panoramax, souveraineté numérique, cartographie publique, France, cartographie collaborative
Read the source article

Quick summary

France's IGN has consolidated its mapping services into Cartes.gouv.fr, a sovereign, collaborative alternative to Google Maps and Street View, with 87% of French citizens supporting state-managed mapping tools independent of US tech giants.

Key takeaways

  • The IGN has grouped all its cartographic services onto a single platform, Cartes.gouv.fr, as a successor to Géoportail and a sovereign alternative to Google Maps and Street View
  • An Ipsos BVA study commissioned by the IGN found 87% of French people consider it essential or important that the State manages public mapping tools independent of American or Chinese multinationals
  • Over 8 in 10 French citizens are prepared to change their habits to do without GAFAM services for mapping
  • Panoramax, the French alternative to Street View, already incorporates 110 million photos contributed collaboratively
  • The platform is part of a broader strategy of digital sovereignty, responding to growing concerns about dependence on Google and Chinese mapping services
